correctness.rationale: The rooted outbreak tails have exact edge-subset Bernstein coefficients. Exhaustive Prüfer enumeration visits every labeled tree at orders 2 through 6, each edge subset, each source, tail threshold, and coefficient; 609408 exact integer differences across 20796 source pairs have zero sign conflicts. Nonnegative Bernstein bases prove one stochastic-order direction uniformly for every \(p\in(0,1)\). On the seven-vertex tree the tails at thresholds two and four have exactly opposite nonzero signs \(p(1-p)\) and \(-p^4(1-p)\) for all \(p\in(0,1)\), giving a sharp failure. Exact rooted subtree generating functions independently reproduce witness p=1/2 law. No infinite theorem beyond stated finite cutoff is inferred.

value.rationale: The sharp minimum seven-vertex construction separates epidemic-source rank by expected burden from rank by probability of a strict-majority outbreak for every transmission probability. A complete lower bound shows the phenomenon cannot occur on a smaller contact tree, making the size a natural exact invariant for source-risk assessment. This is not a merely convenient graph example: it identifies when averages conceal opposite large-outbreak priorities; proof exact and scope transparent.
